segments.say: You step outside, slowly, wrapped in your warm blanket. Behind the cabin, there's a small garden, and the moon is shining over it now, round and silver. Everything is still wet from the rain, so every leaf and petal glitters softly in the moonlight. The air is cool and fresh, and smells of wet earth and flowers. It's very quiet, and very beautiful.

Picture the garden in the moonlight. A narrow stone path, shining wet. Beds of flowers, their petals silvered by the moon. A low hedge, and an old wooden bench at the end of the path. A thin mist hovers just above the grass. Everything looks soft and dreamlike, as if the garden itself were sleeping, and dreaming of the moon.

You walk slowly along the stone path. Each step is soft and careful. The stones are cool beneath your feet. The leaves brush gently against the blanket as you pass. You stop for a moment to look at a single flower, its petals closed for the night, a small drop of rain resting on it like a tiny pearl. Then you walk on, slowly, toward the bench.

You sit down on the old wooden bench and pull the blanket around you. Above you, the clouds have drifted away, and the sky is clear and deep. The moon is bright. And around it, stars are appearing, one by one. You lean back, and look up, and let your eyes rest on the sky. There's nothing else you need to do.

Listen to the night garden. Crickets singing softly in the grass. A raindrop falling from a leaf, with the tiniest sound. An owl, calling once, far away in the forest. And the hush of a gentle breeze, moving through the hedge. Each sound is small and slow, and the silence between them is wide and peaceful.

show.title: Sounds of the night garden
items: A drop falling from a leaf

segments.say: If you watch the moon for a long time, you might notice that it moves. Very, very slowly, it drifts across the sky, from one side of the garden to the other. You can't see it moving in any single moment. But after a while, it's a little further along than it was. That's how the night passes. Not in rushes, but in slow, gentle drifting, almost too slow to see.

Here's a thought for the garden. The moon never hurries, yet it always arrives. It crosses the whole sky every night, without ever rushing, without ever falling behind. Perhaps we can be a little more like the moon. Moving gently through our days, at our own pace, trusting that we'll get where we need to be, in time.

show.text: The moon never hurries, yet it always arrives.

segments.say: Let's count a few stars together, slowly. There's one, bright and white, just above the hedge. One. And another, a little fainter, near the moon. Two. And another, far over the trees. Three. You don't need to count them all. There are far too many. Just let your eyes drift from star to star, softly, one at a time, the way the sand falls in the hourglass.

Picture the sky above the garden. The dark shapes of the treetops at the bottom. Above them, the moon, glowing softly. And everywhere, stars, scattered like sugar across deep blue velvet. Some bright, some faint, some so small you can only see them if you look a little to the side. The sky is so big, and so calm, and so very still.

Some of the light from those stars has been travelling for a very long time to reach your eyes tonight. It set out long before you were born, and crossed unimaginable distances, just to arrive in this quiet garden, at this moment. There's something peaceful about that. The universe is in no hurry. And tonight, neither are you.

Breathe with the night now. In, slowly, as wide and calm as the sky. Out, softly, like the breeze through the hedge. In. And out. Your body is warm in the blanket. Your eyes are heavy. The stars are gentle above you. And everything, the garden, the moon, the night, is resting together with you.

Let's rest in the garden together. A silver moon. Stars above the trees. Crickets singing in the grass. A warm blanket around your shoulders. And a slow, wide breath, as calm as the sky. Everything is peaceful. Everything is still. And sleep is drifting closer now, as softly as the moon across the sky.

You notice that you're very sleepy now. Your head is nodding a little. The blanket feels heavier and warmer. The stars seem to blur together into a soft, silvery glow. It's time to go back inside, and lie down, and sleep. You stand up slowly from the bench, and walk back along the shining path, step by gentle step.

Inside the cabin, there's a small bed in the corner, near the glowing fire, with soft pillows and a thick quilt. You climb in, and the quilt settles over you, warm and heavy. The fire glows low. The window shows a square of moonlit sky. And all around the cabin, the forest is quiet and still, keeping watch over you as you rest.

show.sub: A small bed by the fire

segments.say: And slowly, gently, the cabin and the garden begin to fade, the way dreams do, softly and without a sound. The fire, the quilt, the moonlit window, all dissolve into a warm, peaceful darkness. And you find yourself drifting home, back to your own bed, wherever you are tonight. Warm. Safe. And very nearly asleep.
